capitals.name: Sarmizegetusa Regia
capitals.note: 'Burebista transferred Geto-Dacians capital from Argedava to Sarmizegetusa Regia'; the page gives no year for the move and the Burebista page names no capital, so the whole reign is drawn at Sarmizegetusa. Argedava (the earlier capital) has no coordinates here.

rulers.name: Burebista
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign 82/61-45/44 BC'; Hitchins dates the start of his reign to 82 BC, Bunson, Middleton and Schmitz to about 61-60 BC; killed in a plot of the Dacian aristocracy in 44 BC (other sources 45 or 44 BC).

correction.text: Burebista's Dacia, 'between the Danube, Tisza, and Dniester rivers, covering roughly modern Romania and Moldova'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'A Dacian kingdom that united the Dacians and the Getae was formed under the rule of Burebista in 82 BC' and 'The Dacia of King Burebista (82-44 BC) stretched from the Black Sea to the river Tisza' (Dacia page); Burebista page: 'At its height the kingdom lay between the Danube, Tisza, and Dniester rivers, covering roughly modern Romania and Moldova'. Modern Romania plus Moldova is 260 thousand km2 in the gazetteer; neither page gives an area. The page dates the start of the reign to 82 BC but the Burebista page notes the alternative of about 61-60 BC, from which his conquests run ('From 61 BC onwards').

correction.text: Burebista's Dacia with the Black Sea coast: 'Beginning around 55 BC Burebista annexed the Greek cities' from Olbia to Apollonia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Beginning around 55 BC Burebista annexed the Greek cities' of the Black Sea coast 'from Olbia to Apollonia' (Burebista page). The coast is drawn as Dobruja (north and south), which covers the Black Sea cities of Tomis, Callatis and Dionysopolis but not Olbia (Ukraine) or Apollonia; the pages give no more. The 60/59 BC conquest of the Boii and Taurisci has no place on either page and is not drawn.

region.text: Burebista's Dacia, 'between the Danube, Tisza, and Dniester rivers, covering roughly modern Romania and Moldova'

ledger.note: 82 BC: Burebista founds the Dacian kingdom. 'A Dacian kingdom that united the Dacians and the Getae was formed under the rule of Burebista in 82 BC'; the Burebista page: 'Historian Keith Hitchins dates the start of Burebista's reign to 82 BC', Bunson, Middleton and Schmitz 'about 61-60 BC'; infobox 'Reign 82/61-45/44 BC'. The land is the page's height-of-power extent, not the 82 BC extent.

region.text: the Black Sea coast: 'Beginning around 55 BC Burebista annexed the Greek cities', from Olbia to Apollonia

ledger.counterpart: West Pontic Greek cities (Olbia to Apollonia)
ledger.note: about 55 BC: Burebista annexes the Greek cities of the Black Sea coast. 'Beginning around 55 BC Burebista annexed the Greek cities'; the Black Sea cities were taken 'from Olbia to Apollonia'; Dionysopolis had good relations with him (an inscription of 48 BC calls Akornion his 'first and greatest friend').

region.text: Burebista's Dacia with the Black Sea coast: 'Beginning around 55 BC Burebista annexed the Greek cities' from Olbia to Apollonia

ledger.note: 44 BC: Burebista is killed and the kingdom falls apart. 'In the same year Caesar was assassinated, Burebista was killed in a plot by the Dacian aristocracy' (other sources give 45 BC); 'After Burebista's death, the kingdom was divided into four parts' and 'By the time of Augustus Dacia had broken further into five parts'. Dacia page: 'plunged into internal strife, resembling a civil war'. The pages name none of the parts.

wars.name: Burebista's conquest of the Boii and Taurisci
wars.outcome: 'In 60/59 BC he defeated and conquered the Boii', along with the Taurisci (Burebista page). The pages do not place the land.
wars.note: The boii dossier (eu-03-x) exists; whether these Boii are the people it covers is not on the pages opened, so the slug is a pointer for the reviewer. [Reviewer eu-04-x, 2026-10-19: belligerent changed from the slug boii, whose dossier is the Cisalpine Boii of Italy (-396 to -191), to a name string for the Danubian Boii and Taurisci of 60/59 BC.]

wars.name: Burebista and the Roman civil war
wars.outcome: 'During the Roman civil war of 49-44 BC' Pompey gained Burebista's support through Akornion; Caesar 'ended that alliance at Pharsalus and planned an attack, but was assassinated in 44 BC before it began' (Burebista page). No territorial change.
wars.note: Burebista raided Thrace, Macedonia and Illyria (Burebista page); no land changed hands.

certainty.note: The pages give rivers (Danube, Tisza, Dniester) and the Black Sea as limits; no frontier is surveyed.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks, written in the same batch as dacian-kingdom (Decebalus, 87-106); the two are separated by 130 years of 'four' and then 'five' rival Dacian parts that no page names or places. The two dossiers could be linked as one colour family (balkans) by the colour agent. Two pages opened. The reign start (82 BC or about 61-60 BC) is disputed on the Burebista page. Wikidata id unknown. Counterparts needing dossiers: 'West Pontic Greek cities (Olbia to Apollonia)'. Gazetteer: 'Argedava' (earlier capital) and 'Apollonia Pontica' are unknown names; the Great Hungarian Plain, Pannonian Basin are not region names.
